content.text:
Confirmed: commit `f1939c88` introduced both the `set.remove/set.add` mutation inside `changeAlarm()` (called by `enable()`) and simultaneously switched `disableExpiredAlarms()` from iterating a DB `Cursor` to iterating the in-memory `set` directly, while still calling `enable()` from inside that loop — this creates a `ConcurrentModificationException` since `set` is structurally modified during iteration over itself.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: f1939c88e3f8602b993b1b2e30bda8b4adb34409

## Reasoning
(1) The bug-fixing commit (`62dd6a1`) rewrote `init()`/`checkAlarmIsExpired`-style loop so it calls `alarm.setEnabled(false); writeToDb(alarm.getId());` instead of `enable(alarm.getId(), false)`, and also removed `changeAlarm()`'s `set.remove(alarm); set.add(alarm);` calls (replaced throughout by a plain `writeToDb()`). This signals the bug was: mutating the `set` collection (via `enable()` → `changeAlarm()`) from inside a `for (Alarm alarm : set)` loop, which throws `ConcurrentModificationException`. I traced the history of `Alarms.java`/`AlarmsManager.java` with `git log -p` to find when (a) the loop started iterating over the in-memory `set` and (b) `changeAlarm()` started mutating that same `set`.

(2) In commit `f1939c88e3f8602b993b1b2e30bda8b4adb34409`, `AlarmsManager` was rewritten to cache alarms in an in-memory `Set<Alarm> set` (previously alarms were only queried from the DB via `Cursor`). As part of this same commit, two things changed together:
   - `disableExpiredAlarms()` was changed from iterating a DB `Cursor` to iterating `for (Alarm alarm : set)`, while still calling `enable(alarm.id, false)` inside the loop.
   - `changeAlarm(Alarm alarm)` (invoked by `enable()`) was changed to call `set.remove(alarm); set.add(alarm);`, i.e., it now structurally modifies `set`.

   The combination — iterating `set` with a for-each loop and modifying `set` from inside that loop via `enable()`/`changeAlarm()` — is a classic `ConcurrentModificationException` bug. It persisted through the rename from `AlarmsManager` to `Alarms` (`e86f6cf`) and refactors `506f53e`/`717ab02` (which kept the identical pattern: for-loop over `set` + `enable()` call inside it), until it was finally fixed in `62dd6a1` by avoiding any set mutation inside the loop.

(3) Evidence: `git show f1939c8 -- AlarmsManager.java` shows the Cursor-based loop being replaced by `for (Alarm alarm : set)` in the very same diff hunk where `changeAlarm()` gains `set.remove`/`set.add`. Before this commit, `enable()`'s underlying implementation never touched the `set` field (it didn't exist), so calling it from a loop over a `Cursor` was safe. After this commit, both pieces of the hazardous pattern exist simultaneously, and all subsequent history up to the fix commit preserves this pattern unchanged. I'm confident this single commit is the origin of the bug; I did not find an earlier point where only one of the two necessary ingredients (set-based iteration, set-mutating `enable`) existed in isolation after this point, which also matches the fix commit `62dd6a1` eliminating exactly these two ingredients.
